questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Burkina Faso?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Burkina Faso article.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It is next to Mali, _____, Benin, Togo, Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Mali”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Burkina Faso article.

questions.proof: It is next to Mali, Niger, Benin, Togo, Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It used to be called Upper Volta and the name was changed to Burkina Faso in _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Burkina Faso article.

questions.proof: It used to be called Upper Volta and the name was changed to Burkina Faso in 1984.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The country was once ruled by France, but it has been independent since _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Burkina Faso article.

questions.proof: The country was once ruled by France, but it has been independent since 1960.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “In 1960, Upper Volta became independent from _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “independent”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Burkina Faso article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: In 1960, Upper Volta became independent from France.
